meta.title: The Tree of IRIX 7
meta.description: A living, interactive map of the IRIX 7 operating system roadmap.
intro: IRIX 7 is a clean-room, Rust-native operating system for the SGI Indy: the successor SGI might have built, running IRIX 6.5 binaries unchanged.
The Tree is its living roadmap. The roots are the foundations, the trunk is the control plane, and every branch is a dependency you can follow all the way to a release.
Nothing here is a date. It is a map of what must be true before the next thing can grow.
meta.note: Grown from docs/plan/milestones.md. Statuses sync from the IRIX 7 Roadmap project.

exploring.note: Research and design; the shape may still change.

nodes.title: IRIX 7
nodes.subtitle: IP22 · MIPS R4400
nodes.summary: A clean-room Rust operating system for the SGI Indy, carrying IRIX's identity forward as first-class services.

nodes.title: Toolchain
nodes.summary: A reproducible cross-compilation path for n32/MIPS III and o32/MIPS II, pinned in Nix and gated in CI.
nodes.demo: CI cross-compiles a no_std binary for both targets, and the tracer bullet prints its marker on iris.
criteria: `-Z build-std` builds `core` and `alloc` for both custom targets.
The LLVM path works for n32 and o32; the `rustc_codegen_gcc` path is still pending.
The Nix devshell pins rustc, GCC, binutils and the target specs.
A clean checkout builds the tracer bullet without manual steps.
CI caches the toolchain and the target artefacts.
The build is reproducible (same inputs → same hashes) — still being verified.
nodes.deps: Access to `irix7/project`, the Nix flake, the captured sysroot, iris.
nodes.risks: Host-toolchain glue; GCC-backend disk space; nightly drift.

nodes.title: ROM netboot
nodes.summary: An assembly PROM stub that sizes and tests DRAM, decompresses the n32 kernel to 0x8804_0000 and jumps; the kernel owns Seeq networking, DHCP/DNS/NTP, HTTP/HTTPS, the telnet console and HTTPS-loaded modules.
nodes.demo: In iris the PROM prints the banner, tests 32 MiB, decompresses the kernel and prints `kernel: up`; DHCP/DNS complete, the telnet console answers and survives reboot, and `https example.com:443/` verifies the chain and body digest.
criteria: Serial console works from the first instruction.
RAM is sized and tested stacklessly before any RAM structures exist.
The kernel is decompressed from PROM and entered at 0x8804_0000.
Seeq 8003 + HPC3 PDMA; DHCPv4 with renewals; DNS; NTP; ICMP.
HTTP/1.1 and HTTPS/TLS 1.3 with certificate-chain verification.
SHA-256 over fetched bodies; modules are gated on their digest.
Telnet console survives boot and reconnect.
Modules are fetched over HTTPS into RAM and executed in place.
The image fits in the 512 KiB PROM window (about 476 KiB).
The handoff is documented; BootInfo is optional and the current ROM passes registers.
nodes.deps: M0, iris (or an Indy), a local HTTP server for modules.
nodes.risks: PROM window size; Seeq DMA cache coherency; 80C03 register semantics; 10 Mbit timeouts.

nodes.title: Kernel core
nodes.summary: The privileged framework: traps, TLB, CP0 timer, frames, scheduler, capabilities and a panic path that tells you the truth.
nodes.demo: The kernel prints the ARCS memory map, calibrates the timer, runs two tasks with EDF and fair classes, handles a deliberate page fault, and panics cleanly with a register dump.
criteria: Exception vectors, TLB refill and `eret` work on MIPS III.
CP0 `Count`/`Compare` calibrated against the 8254 reference.
Frame allocator from the ARCS memory descriptor list; no probing.
16 MiB kseg2 mapping works; kseg0 direct map is used for the kernel.
Capability table with generation counters and rights.
EDF and fair run queues; `is_running` debug assertion.
Panic screen with registers, stack trace and a serial dump.
The `ctl`/`data`/`status` driver interface is specified and unit-tested.
nodes.risks: TLB/cache corner cases; exception vector placement; no full IOMMU; stack usage.
nodes.note: The framework boots on iris: frames, scheduler and the CP0 timer/WAIT idle path are live. Remaining: 8254 calibration, page-fault handling, a register-dump panic screen, and the driver interface.

nodes.title: Control plane
nodes.summary: The development harness: a de-privileged network cell, an MCP server and a shell. The control plane is how everything else gets built. Prototype: the httpd module serves MCP initialize/ping/tools/list/tools/call over the module TCP services, with status, echo, console and serial.read tools.
nodes.demo: An agent connects to the Indy over Streamable HTTP with a bearer token, runs `uname`, lists files, reads the serial log, captures the framebuffer, and reboots the machine.
nodes.note: A prototype MCP server runs as modules/httpd on guest port 80 (host 8088): initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call with status, echo, console and serial.read. Bearer auth, SSE, shell and screen/serial tools remain.
criteria: Network cell owns the Seeq, exposes `/net`, and survives a reset.
MCP `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping` and progress notifications.
Tools: `shell.exec`, `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `fs.list`, `serial.read`, `serial.write`, `screen.capture`, `system.reset`, `system.poweroff`.
Bearer token authentication; no TLS in v1; binds to the LAN interface.
Shell: `help`, `ls`, `cat`, `echo`, `uname`, `ps`, `reboot`, `poweroff`.
`system.reset` is guarded by the watchdog and returns after the reboot.
The agent loop is documented and reproducible.
The MCP control plane is a cell, not a kernel thread.
nodes.deps: M2, R2/local HTTP, a host-side MCP client.
nodes.risks: MCP prompt injection; full root; no audit; network driver bugs.

nodes.title: Storage
nodes.summary: Read the root image from R2 over HTTP Range through a userspace block and filesystem stack — with the disk absent or present.
nodes.demo: The shell runs `cat /etc/motd` and `ls /` from the EROFS root image; a write to `/tmp` goes to the overlay; the machine boots with no SCSI disk.
criteria: SCSI cell initialises the WD33C93 and reads blocks.
Block cell exposes a block-device capability and an LRU cache.
EROFS reader mounts the standard little-endian image; byte-order codec tested.
HTTP Range client fetches 64–256 KiB blocks with read-ahead.
SHA-256 verifies the image before mount.
Overlay supports `/tmp`, `/etc`, `/home` (RAM; optional local disk).
The boot path works with the disk absent and with the disk present.
All storage drivers are de-privileged cells.
nodes.risks: SCSI DMA/direction; EROFS corner cases; R2 latency; 10 Mbit throughput.

nodes.title: IRIX binaries
nodes.summary: Run one real IRIX 6.5 o32 binary unchanged: ELF loader, o32 syscall decode, a minimal IRIX libc and the compatibility corpus.
nodes.demo: An o32 `hello` binary from the IRIX 6.5.7m sysroot prints `hello, IRIX 7` and exits with status 0; the shell reports the exit status.
criteria: ELF loader maps the o32 image and its interpreter/libs.
o32 syscall decode: `write`, `exit`, `open`, `close`, `read`, `brk`, `getpid`.
Minimal IRIX libc: `write`, `exit`, `open`, `close`, `read`, `malloc`/`free`, `printf`.
Argument and environment passing; stack layout correct.
`errno` mapping; exit status propagation.
The test binary and expected output are in the compatibility corpus.
The clean-room provenance of the binary and the libc is recorded.
Backward compatibility only: no forward promises.
nodes.risks: ABI details; libc surface; stack/register conventions; big-endian.

nodes.title: Display
nodes.summary: A native display server and a minimal IRIX-inspired desktop: window, text, cursor, damage repair, 8-bit indexed.
nodes.demo: A native window shows `hello, IRIX 7`, moves, raises and redraws with damage tracking; the hardware cursor moves; the desktop has a launcher and a clock.
criteria: Newport REX3 blit, fill, line and text paths work.
VC2 mode programming (1024×768 or 1280×1024) and XMAP9 palette.
Hardware cursor in the XMAP9 auxiliary plane.
Retained window images and damage-driven repair.
Display lease for a full-screen cell.
Input: keyboard and mouse events.
A minimal native desktop: launcher, window manager, clock, terminal.
The display protocol is documented in display-protocol.md.
nodes.risks: Undocumented VRAM size; REX3 FIFO depth; 24-bit planar mode; input.

nodes.title: X11
nodes.summary: Run real IRIX X clients under a clean-room Rust X11 server in display-lease mode.
nodes.demo: `xterm` and `twm` run under X11 on the Indy; the keyboard and mouse work; the server survives an X client crash.
criteria: X11 connection handshake, MSBFirst, setup reply.
Core protocol: windows, GCs, pixmaps, fonts, events, properties, selections.
8-bit PseudoColor and 24-bit TrueColor visuals.
Extensions required by the corpus: SHAPE, MIT-SHM (or a local equivalent), XTEST.
Xlib ABI subset sufficient for `xterm`/`twm`.
Display lease integration with the native display server.
X Test Suite subset passes.
The X11 server is a native cell; legacy clients are MMU processes.
nodes.risks: Xlib/Motif surface; protocol corner cases; performance; 4Dwm parity.

nodes.title: XFS
nodes.summary: Read an IRIX 6.5 XFS v4 disk image: superblock, allocation groups, inodes, extents and the bmap B+tree.
nodes.demo: `ls /mnt/irix` lists an IRIX 6.5 disk image and `cat` reads a file.
criteria: Superblock, AG headers, inode core, extents, bmap B+tree.
Four directory forms, symlinks, clean-log check.
Big-endian metadata; no byte swapping on the hot path.
Refuses a dirty log with a clear message.
Test corpus: clean IRIX 6.5 images, large files, sparse files, symlinks.
`fsck`-style consistency checks for the reader.
The XFS server is a userspace cell over a block-device capability.
No log replay and no write path in v1.0.
nodes.risks: IRIX v4 specifics (v1 dirs, ACLs); dirty logs; corrupted images.

nodes.title: Native cells
nodes.summary: Load and run a native Rust cell through the capability ABI and the Unix-shaped libc.
nodes.demo: A Rust cell opens a file, maps a shared buffer, calls a server over a channel, and prints `hello from a cell`; `fork`/`exec` on a small cell works.
criteria: Cell loader: `.o` relocation, `CellNamespace`, symbol resolution.
Capability table: rights, derivation, delegation, revocation.
Synchronous IPC + shared memory; `Port` events.
Native libc: `open`/`read`/`write`/`close`/`mmap`/`fork`/`exec`/`wait`.
Process = one cell with a Unix personality; fd = capability.
`fork` is limited to small cells; `posix_spawn`/`exec` is the preferred path.
ABI version negotiation; incompatible cells are refused.
The native ABI is documented in native-abi.md.
nodes.risks: `fork` in a SAS kernel; cell relocation; capability/namespace impedance.

nodes.title: Real Indy
nodes.summary: Boot, run and update IRIX 7 on a real Indy from R2: the integration gate where every branch has to hold.
nodes.demo: A real Indy cold-boots from the ROM, fetches the kernel and root image from R2, starts MCP, runs X11, reads an XFS disk, and updates to a new image with rollback.
criteria: Cold boot on both real Indys (or the supported configuration).
Graphics board detection (Newport 8-bit/24-bit; XZ/Extreme if present).
SCSI, Seeq, HAL2, Vino detection and basic operation.
MCP over the real network; watchdog recovery.
X11 `xterm`/`twm` on the real hardware.
XFS read-only on a real IRIX disk.
Image update: fetch, verify, A/B switch, rollback.
Installer/user/admin docs; troubleshooting guide.
SBOM, checksums, signature, release notes.
The release is reproducible from a clean checkout.
nodes.risks: Hardware failures; real-Indy configuration; R2 quotas; last-mile bugs.

nodes.title: Network cell
nodes.summary: A de-privileged cell owns the Seeq 8003, exposes `/net`, and survives a reset without taking the kernel with it.

nodes.title: MCP server
nodes.summary: Streamable HTTP, bearer token, tools for shell, files, serial, screen capture, reset and poweroff.

nodes.title: Agent shell
nodes.summary: A small shell with `help`, `ls`, `cat`, `echo`, `uname`, `ps`, `reboot` and `poweroff` over the control plane.

nodes.title: Watchdog
nodes.summary: The DS1386 watchdog guards `system.reset`; a wedged cell is recovered rather than babysat.

nodes.title: WD33C93 SCSI
nodes.summary: Initialise the WD33C93, read blocks and expose a block-device capability to userspace.

nodes.title: Block cache
nodes.summary: An LRU cache with explicit DMA sync, sized for 10 Mbit reads and a 64 MiB-class machine.

nodes.title: EROFS reader
nodes.summary: Mount the standard little-endian EROFS root image, with a tested big-endian byte-order codec.

nodes.title: HTTP range
nodes.summary: Fetch 64–256 KiB root-image blocks with read-ahead, and verify the image before mount.

nodes.title: ELF loader
nodes.summary: Map an o32 image and its interpreter and libraries with the right stack layout and protections.

nodes.title: o32 syscalls
nodes.summary: Decode the first o32 call set: write, exit, open, close, read, brk and getpid.

nodes.title: IRIX libc
nodes.summary: A minimal clean-room libc: file I/O, memory allocation, printf and errno mapping.

nodes.title: Compat corpus
nodes.summary: Record the test binary, its expected output and its clean-room provenance before it runs.

nodes.title: Newport REX3
nodes.summary: Blit, fill, line and text paths, plus VC2 mode programming and the XMAP9 palette.

nodes.title: Damage repair
nodes.summary: Retained window images and damage-driven redraws, so moving a window does not repaint the world.

nodes.title: Display lease
nodes.summary: A full-screen lease for a cell that wants the framebuffer, with a clean path back to the desktop.

nodes.title: Native desktop
nodes.summary: Launcher, window manager, clock and terminal: IRIX-inspired, not a pixel-for-pixel relic.

nodes.title: X11 core
nodes.summary: Handshake, MSBFirst, windows, GCs, pixmaps, fonts, events, properties and selections.

nodes.title: Xlib subset
nodes.summary: Enough Xlib ABI for `xterm` and `twm`, without pretending to be the whole X ecosystem.

nodes.title: SHAPE + XTEST
nodes.summary: The extensions the corpus actually needs: SHAPE, a local MIT-SHM equivalent and XTEST.

nodes.title: xterm + twm
nodes.summary: Real IRIX clients on the real display path; a client crash must not take the server down.

nodes.title: XFS v4 reader
nodes.summary: Superblock, allocation-group headers, inode cores and the clean-log check.

nodes.title: B+tree extents
nodes.summary: Walk the bmap B+tree and extents without byte-swapping on the hot path.

nodes.title: Dirs + symlinks
nodes.summary: All four directory forms, symlinks and the v1 quirks of an IRIX 6.5 disk.

nodes.title: Clean-log guard
nodes.summary: Refuse a dirty log with a clear message. XFS writes and replay stay in the compost.

nodes.title: Cell loader
nodes.summary: Relocate a `.o`, resolve its `CellNamespace` and load it into a fresh capability domain.

nodes.title: Capability rights
nodes.summary: Rights, derivation, delegation and revocation — with generation counters that make stale handles loud.

nodes.title: IPC + ports
nodes.summary: Synchronous IPC, shared memory and port events: the native equivalent of a syscall surface.

nodes.title: Native libc
nodes.summary: A Unix-shaped libc where a process is one cell and a file descriptor is a capability.

nodes.title: Developer harness
nodes.summary: Serial, network, MCP, shell, reset and watchdog — the machine becomes programmable.

nodes.title: First IRIX binary
nodes.summary: One real IRIX 6.5 binary runs unchanged, with a minimal libc and a compatibility corpus.

nodes.title: Native desktop
nodes.summary: Newport display, a native window system and a small IRIX-inspired desktop.

nodes.title: X11
nodes.summary: A clean-room X11 server in display-lease mode, running `xterm` and `twm`.

nodes.title: XFS read-only
nodes.summary: Read a real IRIX 6.5 XFS disk image, with a clean-log guard and no write path.

nodes.title: Native cells
nodes.summary: Native Rust cells, a capability ABI and a Unix-shaped native libc.

nodes.title: Real Indy
nodes.summary: A real Indy as a daily driver: cold boot from R2, MCP, X11, XFS and signed A/B updates.

nodes.title: Clean-room provenance
nodes.summary: Harness-enforced provenance, similarity screening, DCO and access control for the private source tree.

nodes.title: CI + automation
nodes.summary: Cross-build, emulator boot, smoke harness, hardware-in-the-loop and releases.

nodes.title: Documentation
nodes.summary: The book, the interface specs, install and troubleshooting guides, ADRs and this tree.

nodes.title: Security
nodes.summary: Threat model, MCP modes, supply-chain gates and vulnerability disclosure.

nodes.title: Hardware lab
nodes.summary: Two Indys, serial, SCSI emulation, spares and backups — the only real proof that matters.

nodes.title: Performance
nodes.summary: Benchmarks tracked over time, never used as a merge gate.

nodes.title: Community
nodes.summary: Contributing, governance, good-first issues and release notes that tell the truth.

nodes.title: ISDN
nodes.summary: The Indy's ISDN option is not in v1.0.
nodes.reason: Rare hardware, no test target and no user story. The compost is the right place.

nodes.title: Indy Video
nodes.summary: Video output is deferred until the real boards are probed.
nodes.reason: The video path needs hardware we cannot yet characterise. It waits outside v1.0.

nodes.title: 3D acceleration
nodes.summary: No GL or GLX acceleration in v1.0.
nodes.reason: 2D display and X11 compatibility come first; accelerating 3D is a different project.

nodes.title: XFS writes
nodes.summary: XFS is read-only; log replay and write-back are out.
nodes.reason: A read-only compatibility server is the smaller, honest promise. Data integrity first.

nodes.title: GLX + rootless X
nodes.summary: X11 is lease-based; GLX and rootless embedding are out.
nodes.reason: The corpus needs `xterm` and `twm`, not a full X desktop compositor.

nodes.title: Full POSIX
nodes.summary: The native ABI is capability-first, not POSIX-first.
nodes.reason: The Unix shape is a compatibility surface, not the native design centre.

nodes.title: I7FS in v1.0
nodes.summary: A new on-disk format is not a v1.0 dependency.
nodes.reason: EROFS and read-only XFS carry v1.0. I7FS is a later experiment.

nodes.title: Indigo Magic parity
nodes.summary: The new desktop is IRIX-inspired, not a pixel-for-pixel recreation.
nodes.reason: The goal is a good native desktop, not a museum exhibit.

nodes.title: Forward compatibility
nodes.summary: Native IRIX 7 binaries will not run on IRIX 6.5.
nodes.reason: Backward compatibility is the mandate. Forward compatibility is explicitly out.
